newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei stages sharp rebound, MSCI Taiwan slow.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei stages sharp rebound, MSCI Taiwan slow.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures staged a fierce rebound in late Monday trade, in line with strong gains on the underlying Tokyo stock market, but dealers said sentiment remained weak and the recovery could be short-lived.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract added a hefty 930 points to close at 18,105 after trading in a volatile 1,210-point range, which took it briefly below the psychological 17,000 support.
In Tokyo, the 225-share Nikkei average ended up 815.14 points, or 4.71 percent, at 18,118.79.

Dealers said the recovery was largely driven by technical factors on both the cash and futures markets, though the dollar's stable tone against the yen and a rebound in banking shares also provided support.
"A corrective rebound was expected after Friday, but I never expected it to bounce so high," said a trader with a local house. The March Nikkei lost almost 1,000 points on Friday.
"The close above 18,000 shows it's at least stabilised the downtrend for now. But we'd need to get above 19,550 to see a trend reversal," he added.
A dealer with a European futures house said there was talk that Japanese public funds were behind some of the buying.
"I think it should come down again. It's gone up too fast," he said, adding that the March Nikkei would encounter strong selling interest above 18,300.
MSCI Taiwan stock index futures had a slow day as even participation by locals dwindled in the face of hectic activity in the Nikkei trading pit, dealers said.
"The Taiwan futures were stifled. I've been placing orders and then cancelling them because there's no movement," said the trader with the local house, citing a lack of market volatility.
The March MSCI Taiwan index contract settled at 310.4 against its opening 307.5 on low turnover of 426 lots.
